basisOfRecord.quote: We studied bee communities in two habitats essential for pollinators (residential gardens and semi-natural areas) at 42 sites situated at the edge of greater Montreal, Canada.
Two of the three collectors were randomly chosen to sample bees with sweep nets during a 30-min period.
We cross-referenced interpretations with data from the Quebec Forest Inventory Service (RNF 2000) and later verified them in the field from August 22–25, 2012.

lifeStage.quote: All bees that were caught were either identified and released while on site - honey bees (Apis mellifera) and most bumble bee (Bombus) species - or frozen and identified later.

measurementStatistic.quote: The floral host of each captured bee was recorded.

The three metrics of bee diversity all responded in the same way to urbanization in both habitat types.
In fact, bee abundance and functional diversity were the same in both ruderal areas and gardens irrespective of landscape context.
